title: Speculative Futures on ChatGPT and Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI): A Collective Reflection from the Educational Landscape
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the rapidly emerging debate around ChatGPT and generative AI in education, asking what future educational possibilities and risks these tools may create. Rather than testing an intervention empirically, the authors use speculative methodology and collective writing to generate fictional future narratives that explore both positive and negative educational scenarios.

The article draws on a globally diverse group of educational scholars who each wrote speculative narratives from different contexts and perspectives. The narratives imagine AI supporting personalized learning, translation and language development, accessibility for students with disabilities, assessment support, and communication across languages and distances. They also imagine risks such as plagiarism, dependence on AI, privacy and ethics concerns, algorithmic bias, inequity in access, and possible erosion of human agency and teacher roles.

The paper is not a study of a single student population or school setting; instead, it is a reflective theoretical piece aimed at the broader educational landscape. Its main conclusion is that generative AI in education is context-dependent and full of both promise and risk, and that educators and policymakers need to develop new literacies, rethink assessment, and keep human agency central when adopting AI technologies.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI / large language model chatbot used for text generation, question answering, summarization, translation, feedback, and other language-based tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper is a speculative/future-oriented reflection centered on ChatGPT and similar generative AI tools in education; it also includes fictional narratives generated by ChatGPT and discusses potential educational uses and risks.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a speculative and theoretical collective reflection, not an empirical evaluation of ChatGPT or any other AI tool. It provides no study design, measures, or outcomes that would support causal or correlational evidence grading beyond opinion/speculation.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues that ChatGPT could have broad educational usefulness, but these are prospective claims rather than measured impacts. Because no effect sizes or outcome data are reported, impact cannot be established empirically.
